text.p: Following are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Pakistani economic managers have reached Washington to see through the $160 million payments deal with the IMF and negotiate a $200 million World Bank loan for banking reforms.
- Bidding for a 26 percent stake in the 880-MW Jamshoro Power Plant will be held in the second week of January.
- Islamic Taleban militia leaders in Afghanistan held talks with Pakistan officials on Sunday and gave a go-ahead for a gas pipeline and rail link between Pakistan and Central Asia.
- The government has agreed to collect 368 billion rupees of revenue and build a reserve level of $1.6 billion by June 30 under the reactivated standby arrangement with the IMF.
- The cement industry asked the government to announce a relief package to save the industry from collapse.
- Banks and development finance institutions are not providing credits for projects approved by their executive boards.

- The Mehran Bank report has revealed transfer of 499 million rupees to 39 account holders through Asset Investment Bank without the consent of depositors, besides huge illegal loan advances that led to the bank's collapse.
- The state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan will export rice worth $10 million to Iraq.
- The government intends to bring private sector professionals into the state-run Privatisation Commission.
- Major General Sikander Hayat, a serving army officer, has been appointed chairman of state-run Pakistan Steel Mills.

- The chairman of the Central Board of Revenue said the government was evaluating the working of pre-shipment inspection companies and a decision to scrap the pre-inspection system will be taken in consultation with leading trade bodies and companies.
- Iran has asked India to resolve its political problems with Pakistan to enable a proposed $5.0 billion gas pipeline project from Iran to India via Pakistan to get under way.
